title: Compact boarding compose guide and signal rubric
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, practitioner-facing guide for closing and bringing new engineers and product hires online quickly with predictable skill signals. It combines: 1) a hiring plan for short-cycle roles, 2) an interview rubric formatted for fast calibration, and 3) a lightweight onboarding checklist focused on first-contribution outcomes. Goal: reduce time-to-first-merge while keeping hiring signal quality high.

High-level hiring plan (how we prioritize and staff)
- Role buckets: core infra (serving/runtime), platform infra, product (console/SDK), SRE/ops.
- Priority cadence: open critical infra roles first (backfill when risk > 2 people out), product roles scheduled as feature milestones approach.
- Hiring velocity targets: two-stage funnel (screen -> takehome OR pair exercise -> final loop). Aim for 3 interviews within 7 business days of screen pass.
- Sourcing brief: include clear example workload (mini task) in outreach so candidates self-select for applied problem-solving.

Interview flow and concise rubric (for quick scoring)
- Stage 0: Recruiter screen (culture fit + logistics) — pass/fail notes.
- Stage 1: Takehome or paired 90m problem aligned to role (code + short design). Provide a template for evidence and time-box review to <48h.
- Stage 2: Technical loop (60–75m) x2: one system-design/architecture, one implementation/debugging + troubleshooting.
- Stage 3: Hiring manager + comp/career match (~40m) and final debrief.

Rubric (single-page, 1–5 scale; calibrate to shared anchors):
- Problem decomposition (weight 30%) — anchors: 5 = clarifies constraints, proposes decomposed components and tradeoffs; 3 = reasonable decomposition but misses edge constraints; 1 = jumps to code without design.
- Correctness & clarity (weight 25%) — anchors: 5 = clear, correct solution and tests; 3 = edge-case gaps; 1 = incorrect/unguided.
- System thinking & tradeoffs (weight 20%) — anchors: 5 = thoughtful capacity/latency/cost tradeoffs; 3 = basic awareness; 1 = no system considerations.
- Communication & collaboration (weight 15%) — anchors: 5 = proactive clarifying, receptive to hints; 3 = adequate; 1 = poor partnerability.
- Ownership signal & impact fit (weight 10%) — anchors: 5 = has examples of shipping ownership; 3 = plausible; 1 = no evidence.

How to score and pass threshold:
- Composite score = weighted average. Pass bar = >=3.6 AND no category <2.
- Fast-fail triggers: evidence of unsafe code practices, misaligned values, inability to reason about production tradeoffs.
- Calibration note: run weekly 30m calibration sync when hiring multiple roles in parallel. Share two anonymized scored packets for alignment.

Candidate experience timeline (commitments we make)
- Recruiter intro within 48 hours of application.
- Takehome or paired slot scheduled within 3 business days of screen pass.
- Full loop completed within 10 business days of takehome return.
- Offer discussion within 48 hours of final decision.
- Transparency: always send debrief summary + improvement suggestions to candidates who ask.

Pre-boarding checklist (T-7 to T-1)
- Access: request laptop imaging, necessary cloud accounts, Slack + calendar invites, basic repo read access.
- Welcome packet: team org chart, first-week schedule, short reading list (arch overview), first-merge expectations doc.
- Manager tasks: 1:1 calendar block for first 6 weeks, assign buddy, prepare small first-sprint ticket.

Day 0 and week 1 (outcomes we measure)
- Day 0: orient (HR basics, IT handoff), join core team standup, get dev env green (first run of test suite).
- Week 1 outcomes: merge a micro-change (docs, lint fix, or tiny bug) and successfully run full local reproduction for a shipped service.
- Success signals: PR merged with reviewer feedback addressed; demonstrates end-to-end developer loop.

Consolidation phase (weeks 2–6)
- Weeks 2–6 outcomes: take ownership of a non-trivial bug or a small feature; present a 10-minute ‘‘context map’’ of the service and deployment path by week 4.
- Manager checkpoints: weekly 1:1, mid-point growth notes at week 3, formal 6-week check-in to set 90-day plan.

Buddy program and micro-mentoring
- Buddy assigned at start; buddy checklist: 1) repo tour, 2) observability runbook demo, 3) deploy walkthrough, 4) first-code-review expectations.
- Encourage short shadow sessions (30m) twice in week 1.

Practical interview artifacts to keep in packet
- Short takehome template (goal, open input test cases, success criteria, time budget).
- Interviewer cheat-sheet (top 6 probing questions per category).
- Debrief template (scores, qualitative notes, suggested role fit).

Common failure modes and mitigations
- Slow scheduling: reserve recurring blocks on hiring teams’ calendars to avoid reschedule churn.
- Reviewer fatigue: mandate single-pass reviews for takehomes with a 48h grading SLA and an escalation path.
- Noise in rubric: anonymize candidate names in calibration packets; use 2 independent reviewers for any score within 0.6 standard deviation.

Operational TODO (notes to self)
- Build a short Confluence page with anonymized exemplar packets for calibration (owner: Aisha).
- Ask engineering leads for a shortlist of 6 micro-first-sprint tickets per team that are safe for new joiners.
- Trial timing experiment: pilot 48h takehome grading window for next 10 hires and measure offer velocity lift.

Open questions for leadership
- Do we require takehomes for senior staff-eng levels? (tradeoffs: signal vs. candidate drop-off)
- Standardize compensation ranges on offer packet to reduce negotiation cycles?

References and links
- See hiring cadence ideas in JIRA-HIRE-88 and the interview-kit in GitHub link above.

Quick notes: this doc is intentionally short-form and pragmatic. Use it as a living working packet for people-ops + hiring managers; copy into candidate-facing templates where appropriate and iterate after each hiring cohort.
